videos.description:
How do you tune a full FTC autonomous in 5 minutes? I sat down with Baron Henderson, co-founder of Pedro Pathing, to talk about how Pedro started, why it exists, what's new in Pedro 3 (Foresight + auto-tuning), and the lessons he's learned building one of the most-used path-following libraries in FTC.

Whether you're a rookie programmer trying to get your first auto working or a top team pushing for extra cycles, this one's for you.

BioBuzz's Corners Might Be a HUGE Problem #FTC #BioBuzz #robocodex #firsttechchallenge
videos.description:
I think the corners of the BioBuzz field might be way more important than people realize. 👀
FIRST has already told us pollen will naturally roll toward the walls and into the corners, which means having a fast intake might not be enough.
The real question is: can your robot actually collect the pollen the field gives you?
That could completely change how teams design their intakes and drivetrain strategy.
What do you think will be the best way to handle corners? 👇

videos.description:
I don’t think FTC teams should be designing their BioBuzz robot yet.

Before kickoff, we don’t know enough to lock in a full design. Instead, build small prototypes, test specific problems, and collect real data.

By kickoff, you should have answers—not guesses.

videos.title: 5 FTC Programming Mistakes Every New Programmer Makes
videos.description:
Welcome to RoboCodex — Robotics Programming, FTC Tutorials, and STEM Projects.

This season completely changed the way our FTC team programmed robots. We didn't become the best team overnight, but we learned lessons that transformed our autonomous from relying on timers and hope to using localization, PedroPathing, finite state machines, telemetry, and vision processing.

In this video, I break down the 5 biggest FTC programming mistakes our team made this season, how we fixed them, and what every new FTC programmer can learn from our experience.

Whether you're just getting started with FTC programming or looking to build a more reliable autonomous, I hope this video saves you some of the mistakes we made.

Subscribe for more FTC programming tutorials, robotics projects, and STEM content!

What You'll Learn

• Why timer-based autonomous eventually breaks down

• How PedroPathing improved our autonomous

• Why PID and localization matter

• How subsystem architecture simplified our code

• Why finite state machines made our robot faster

• How telemetry made debugging dramatically easier

• The biggest programming mindset shift we learned this season

videos.title: The LEGO Education Partnership is Over (FTC is Next)
videos.description:
Why I'm Moving to FIRST Tech Challenge (FTC)

For the past few years, RoboCodex has been focused on FIRST LEGO League (FLL), but it's time for the next chapter.

In this video, I explain why the LEGO Education and FIRST partnership is coming to an end, what that means for FIRST LEGO League after the 2026–2027 season, and why RoboCodex is transitioning to FIRST Tech Challenge (FTC).

This isn't a goodbye to the FLL community—it's the next step in my own robotics journey. I'll also share what kind of content you can expect on the channel going forward and give you a preview of my upcoming FTC Nationals season breakdown.

Join the RoboCodex Community

💬 Discord: https://discord.gg/j5qHDePZF6

📺 Subscribe for upcoming FTC videos, programming tutorials, robot design, strategy, CAD, Java, vision systems, competition insights, and behind-the-scenes content from our team's journey.
